target.title: fix(gateway-client): clamp readiness timeout before client start
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers using an explicit gateway client readiness timeout could pass an oversized finite value that reached the readiness waiter without the safe timer clamp used by the default timeout path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The explicit timeout path now reuses the existing finite timeout delay resolver with the same zero-minimum boundary before starting the client. This keeps the gateway-client readiness boundary local and avoids adding new config, fallback behavior, or broader policy.

## User Impact

Developers can pass explicit readiness timeouts without accidentally forwarding timer values above the safe Node.js delay range to injected or custom readiness waiters.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: explicit gateway client readiness timeouts are clamped to the shared safe timer maximum before invoking the readiness waiter.
- Current-head proof at 238a69ab44fe6b5ff50558f55ce462d6ae5de2de: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-client/src/readiness.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 2 tests passing in `E:\code\openclaw-lane-e`.
- PR diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the focused regression shows `timeoutMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` reaches the waiter as `MAX_SAFE_TIMEOUT_DELAY_MS`, and the client still starts after readiness succeeds.
